title: Quantized Model Memory Leak Forensics + SLO Impact Playbook
author: Claire Nguyen
content:
Overview
--------
This playbook defines a standard, operationalized investigation and mitigation path for memory leaks observed in quantized model serving stacks. It ties the technical forensic steps to SLO impact assessment, error-budget remediation, and capacity decisions. Use this when serving instances running quantized models (INT8/4/LLM quantization variants) exhibit progressive memory growth, OOM cascades, or unexplained eviction behavior.

Scope
-----
- Applies to Redwood Inference internal serving clusters and private deployments where quantized kernels (qint8/q4 variants) are used.
- Covers detection, immediate mitigation, evidence capture, root-cause forensics, SLO impact estimation, and post-incident remediation.
- Not a replacement for the OOM cascade runbook (link above); this document focuses on leak patterns that are slow-burning and correlated with quantized-mode memory paths.

Summary of intent
------------------
- Rapidly stabilize customer-facing SLOs (p95 latency, availability) while preserving forensic evidence.
- Collect minimal viable artifacts to reproduce and attribute leaks to code, kernel, model, or workload patterns.
- Provide a repeatable SLO-impact template so product and SRE can agree on credits/remediation.

Signals that trigger this playbook
--------------------------------
- Sustained monotonic increase in per-container RSS (>= 5% upward trend over 30m) for quantized-serving pods.
- Repeated node-level swap activity or kernel OOM events tied to inference processes.
- Elevated OOM kill rate for model-serving processes without concurrent CPU/IO spikes.
- P95/P99 latency regressions with correlated allocation-growth metrics (kv-cache residency anomalies).
- Alerts: qserv.memory-growth-alert, qserv.swap-activity-warning, qserv-oom-trend-signal.

Owner and escalation
--------------------
- Primary: eng-sre-model-serving oncall (pager: #sre-model-serving).
- Secondary: eng-serving-runtime team (owners: runtime-kernel-leads).
- Escalation timeline: 0–10m stabilize, 10–45m evidence collection, 45–120m mitigation & capacity decisions.

Immediate stabilization (first 0–10 minutes)
--------------------------------------------
1. Mark incident and notify affected stakeholders: SRE, Runtime, Customer Success for impacted tenants.
2. Toggle conservative autoscale policy: set autoscale.max_replicas = current_replicas + 1 and autoscale.scale_cooldown = 300s.
3. Enable per-tenant token-priority throttling for noisy tenants (if enabled): apply policy: priority_level = 0 for background jobs.
4. If OOMs are ongoing, move traffic off affected nodes: cordon node(s) and use drift-safe drain (--graceful 120s).
5. If immediate rollback candidate exists (kernel patch or quantization fallback), follow canary rollback procedure: roll back 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 15m observation windows.

Evidence collection (10–45 minutes) — minimal reproducible set
-----------------------------------------------------------
Collect artifacts in order of decreasing volatility. Preserve timestamps and correlate to SLO telemetry.
- Process snapshots: `pstree -paw` and `pmap -x <PID>` for inference workers.
- Heap/allocator traces: run jemalloc profiling snapshot (if enabled): `MALLOC_CONF=prof:true,lg_prof_interval:22` and `jeprof` capture.
- Kernel dmesg and /var/log/kern.log (capture last 1h): `journalctl --since "1 hour ago" -u qserv`
- Runtime internal counters: kv-cache hits/misses, kv-cache checksum drift, per-request KV-residency (expose via /debug/metrics).
- GPU memory accounting (if hybrid host/GPU leak suspected): `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv` and `rocm-smi --showdrm` as applicable.
- Environment: `pip freeze` for deployed runtime image, quantization lib versions, and /etc/ld.so.cache listing.
- Core dumps: enable temporary core collection: `sysctl -w kernel.core_pattern=/var/crash/qserv-%e.%p.core` and capture compress+hash.
- Container runtime traces: `ctr logs`, `docker inspect`, and `runc exec --log`.

Evidence checklist (mark during incident)
---------------------------------------
- [ ] Process memory growth graph (30m window) for affected containers
- [ ] Kernel OOM/kill events matched to pids
- [ ] jemalloc/allocator profile snapshot keyed to timestamp
- [ ] Quantization kernel version and symbol map
- [ ] Sample request payload(s) that reproduce the growth (anonymized)
- [ ] GPU memory trace if applicable
- [ ] Core dump(s) or tcmalloc/heap profile files uploaded to incident storage

Forensics deep dive (45–240 minutes)
------------------------------------
1. Reproduce locally in isolated canary: spin a canary cluster with identical runtime image, model shard, and quantization flags. Replay captured sample requests (use replay harness described below).
2. If leak reproduces, increment debug levels to trace allocations with symbolized stacks. Use `gdb` on a live pid if safe, or `perf record -g` for offline analysis.
3. Compare allocator profiles across quantized vs. non-quantized variants to isolate kernel vs. runtime allocator differences.
4. Correlate KV-cache eviction patterns with memory growth — are cached prefixes not being released due to a reference counting bug?
5. Validate third-party kernel/wasm/FP16 libs: check known CVEs and prior bug reports.

Telemetry and queries (examples)
-------------------------------
- Per-pod memory growth: PromQL: rate(container_memory_usage_bytes{job=\"qserv\"}[5m]) > 0 and increase(container_memory_usage_bytes{job=\"qserv\"}[30m]) > (0.05 * avg_over_time(container_memory_usage_bytes{job=\"qserv\"}[30m]))
- OOM kill spikes: increase(kube_pod_container_status_terminated_reason{reason=\"OOMKilled\"}[10m]) > 0
- Allocation hotspots: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (source_file) (increase(allocator_alloc_ns_bucket[15m])))

Replay harness (how to reproduce safely)
--------------------------------------
1. Use the incident replay cluster (namespace: replay-<incident_id>) with isolated quota and no production traffic.
2. Replay requests using the capture: `replay-cli --source s3://incidents/<id>/trace.json --concurrency 1 --rate 50/s --target qserv-canary:8080`
3. Run heap/jemalloc profiling concurrently and stream profiles to incident S3.

SLO impact assessment template
-----------------------------
- Affected SLOs: list (example: text-generation p95 latency, embedder availability 99.9)
- Window: <start_ts> to <end_ts>
- Measured breach: metric, observed value, SLO threshold, breach duration
- Error-budget consumption: estimated tokens/requests impacted and % of monthly budget consumed
- Customer-impact summary: tenant IDs, request classes, any credit/refund recommendations

Capacity & error budget decisions (playbook rules)
-------------------------------------------------
- If incident causes <= 1% monthly error-budget consumption and is contained within 3h, document remediation and continue normal SLO governance.
- If > 1% but <= 5% and mitigation requires capacity headroom > 10%, initiate temporary capacity carveout: reserve burst pool with preemptible capacity and update SLO ticketing.
- If > 5% or multi-tenant widespread, invoke emergency capacity protocol and prioritize critical tenants per tenant-priority-matrix.

Mitigation options (ranked)
--------------------------
1. Software workaround: enable quantization-fallback flag (runtime will load float16 kernel path) for affected model versions. Rollout via canary.
2. Hotpatch: apply small allocator-fix if available following the emergency hotpatch checklist.
3. Traffic shaping: strip long-response/chain requests with advisory header X-Redwood-Degrade: true.
4. Capacity: spin dedicated warm-pool nodes with larger headroom, prefer nodes with increased host memory ratio.

Post-incident remediation (48–90 days cycle)
-------------------------------------------
- Short term (0–7d): merge temporary rollback or flag as permanent with test coverage.
- Medium term (7–30d): add synthetic canaries that exercise edge-case quantized paths and run daily memory-regression checks.
- Long term (30–90d): schedule allocator/quantization kernel code review, fuzzing harness for prefix eviction logic, and a SLA review with Product for model owners.

Incident review responsibilities and artifacts to attach
-----------------------------------------------------
- Incident lead: SRE oncall — produce TL;DR and timeline within 24h.
- Runtime owner: provide kernel-level analysis and patch plan.
- Attachments: all artifacts from Evidence checklist, replay traces, reproduction guide, and SLO impact template.

Runbook commands and helpers (copyable snippets)
------------------------------------------------
- Capture processes: `kubectl -n <ns> exec -it <pod> -- pmap -x 1 > /tmp/pmap-$(date +%s).txt`
- Enable temporary jemalloc prof: `kubectl -n <ns> exec <pod> -- env MALLOC_CONF=prof:true jeprof -d /tmp/profiles`
- Create replay namespace: `kubectl create ns replay-<incident_id> && kubectl apply -f replay-quota.yaml -n replay-<incident_id>`

Configuration table (critical thresholds)
----------------------------------------
| Signal | Threshold | Action |
| container_memory_delta_30m | > 5% | Trigger qserv.memory-growth-alert and start forensic snapshotting |
| kube_oom_kills_10m | > 1 | Cordon node, begin immediate traffic shift |
| p95_latency_increase_15m | > 20% | Enable token-priority throttling for noisy tenants |

(When adding thresholds, notify observability owners to validate noise sensitivity and false-positive rates.)

Prevention checklist (for platform roadmap)
-----------------------------------------
- Add memory-leak unit tests for quantized kernels in CI and nightly leak-detection job.
- Expand canary matrix to include mixed-quantization request shapes (long prefix + multi-tool calls).
- Bake allocator-coverage into runtime fuzzing for prefix reference cycles.
- Maintain a compatibility map of quantization library versions to kernel symbols.

Appendix: common root causes observed historically
------------------------------------------------
- Reference-counting regression in kv-cache when using compressed representation.
- jemalloc arena fragmentation with long-lived small allocations from quantized kernel.
- Third-party quantization library holding persistent GPU host-side buffers.
- Lazy deserialization bug: repeated small allocations that are never freed due to exception paths.
